name: Information found by chance
papers: garud2011-65d6ed; krumboltz1998-d53ff4; lane2020-d1934e; merton2004-abf53f; shane2000-cc1be0; vonhippel2016-a67f44
what: The founder comes across an article, a website or a technique while doing something else, and it sparks the idea.
note: Meets the three rules: one clear idea; bears on the research question; no trigger names information found by chance. Drafted code trigger-20, 6 papers.

name: External shock or platform change
what: Something outside the venture changes suddenly: a recession, a platform's policy or algorithm, a supplier ending a tool.

name: Idea from the founder's own experience
what: The idea comes from the founder's own errand, thought or idle play, with no outside input.

name: Unsought publicity from a third party or platform
what: A YouTuber, an influencer or a platform (App Store, Shopify) promotes the product on its own initiative, with no request or offer to the founder.
note: Meets the three rules: one clear idea; bears on the research question; 2.5 is an offer made to the founder, while promotion is aimed at someone else's audience. Inductive: no paper read states it as a trigger. Two of four cases are clean; to be judged mainly on round 2.

name: Outside timing or circumstance
what: A wider change or a life event makes the moment right: maturing technology, a market turning to the founder's skills, a hurricane cleanup, a layoff.

name: Resources, contacts or knowledge as the result
papers: balzano2022-f16721; busch2020-10a2b8; copeland2023-f96149; fultz2025-202492; klyver2025-7a51e3; granovetter1973-32994d; krumboltz1998-d53ff4; giustiniano2016-0b0ee9; lane2020-d1934e
what: What comes of it is a supplier, a network of contacts, customer insights or new connections, not a product, market or growth.
note: Meets the three rules: one clear idea; bears on the research question; the outcome codes name a product, a market, growth or nothing. One code from drafted codes outcome-13, outcome-14 and outcome-17.

name: Harmful result
what: The event costs the venture: a lost channel, half of income gone, survival threatened.
note: Meets the three rules: one clear idea; bears on the research question; the study covers bad surprises; no outcome code names harm. Drafted code outcome-30.

name: Outsider or naive start
what: Not knowing an industry is told as an advantage: never having worked in a law firm, naivety as a superpower.

name: The opportunity found them
what: The founder tells the start as the opportunity finding them, without using luck words.

name: Effort-only account
what: The founder credits results wholly to work put in, with no role for chance.

name: Breakthroughs noticed by founders close to customers
what: A general theory from the founder: things start working through unplanned shifts that only founders close to customers notice.

name: Limiting exposure to chance
what: The founder deliberately screens out incoming opportunities to stay focused.

name: A mission that draws people
what: A nonprofit status and a resonant vision draw volunteers and trust.

name: Find improved the product
what: A chance find fixed the product's core design after founding, without growth or a change of direction.

name: Change in technology, rules or platforms
papers: alvarez2007-c77d51; cattani2005-691ffb; davidsson2015-c4ba86; garud2011-65d6ed; ma2002-d85f40; mcmullen2006-78cdcc; mintzberg1985-9d4ec0; mintzberg1985-df70c8; vanlent2023-afed1a
what: A change outside the founder's control in technology, rules or a platform the venture depends on opens a door or causes a setback: AI maturing, an iOS or search-engine update, a supplier dropping a tool.
note: Meets the three rules: one clear idea; bears on the research question; no trigger names a change in the world outside the founder. Drafted code trigger-12, widened to setbacks and platforms.

name: Outside crisis or disaster
papers: fultz2025-202492; garud2003-926111; garud2014-a2d9b1; ma2002-d85f40; merton2004-abf53f; mirvahedi2017-ff1fb5
what: A sudden, large outside event, such as a recession or a hurricane, opens an opportunity or threatens the venture.
note: Meets the three rules: one clear idea; bears on the research question; the study covers bad surprises. Drafted code trigger-11. Two cases.

name: Personal misfortune
what: A setback in the founder's own life, such as losing a job, sets off the venture.

name: Setback retold as a turning point
what: The founder retells a setback, such as a layoff, a lost client, a failure or a slow start, as the moment that made the business.

name: The venture threatened or reshaped
what: The event neither started, redirected nor advanced the venture: it threatened its survival, changed who ran it or changed how the founder works.

name: Unbidden attention at the edge of 2.10
what: Others' attention came unasked but outside the wording of 2.10: peers noticing results, influencers joining the founder's own affiliate programme, a search engine ranking the founder's post.

name: Legal claim from a third party
what: An outsider's lawsuit or legal action forces a change.

name: Sudden free time
what: A cancelled job or a lost job leaves the founder with time that lets the idea surface or be worked on.

name: Setback from a supplier or the founder's own choice
what: An operational setback: a carrier's delay, or a cost-saving choice that backfires.

name: Another person's decision changes the founder's situation
what: Someone else's decision, such as a boss starting a new venture or a teacher's instruction, changes the founder's situation and sets the story off.

name: Disaster as the setting for a chance
what: A disaster put the founder where a chance encounter happened; coded as a condition, not as the trigger 2.7.

name: A customer's misfortune scatters contacts
what: A client firm's near collapse moved known contacts into new firms, which became customers.

name: Change in a market outside the venture
what: An outside supply event, such as a famous mine closing, shifts demand.

name: Adversity as a push
what: Losing a customer pushed the founder to look again at suppliers and buyers.

name: Lessons from past failures
what: Past failures taught the founder to launch fast and test.

name: Competing life commitments
what: Another commitment, such as waiting for a military call-up, made the founder neglect the venture.

name: A skill that built the audience
what: A skill of the founder's built the following that later drew requests.

name: Founding to learn
what: The venture was started mainly as a way to learn, not to build a business.

name: Founding told second-hand
what: The founding is told by someone who did not live it, which bears on how far its surprise and search state can be trusted.

name: Self-critical account of pivots
what: The founder credits pivots with building the business but warns others against pivoting.

name: A name or identity as the result
what: What came of it was the business's name or identity.

name: Goodwill as the result
what: What came of it was an audience's goodwill and engagement.

name: Demand that overwhelms
what: A sudden rush of demand overloaded the operation, with no stated gain or loss.
